title: Sum Root to Leaf Numbers
summary: Given a binary tree with digit nodes, calculate the sum of all numbers formed by root-to-leaf paths.
statement: Given a binary tree with digit nodes, calculate the sum of all numbers formed by root-to-leaf paths. Each path represents a number, and the sum of these numbers is returned. A leaf node has no children.
constraints: 1–1000 nodes, each holding a digit 0–9. Tree depth is at most 10.
The total answer fits a signed 32-bit integer. Count only complete root-to-leaf paths.

hints: A path's numeric prefix can be carried from parent to child.
Append a digit with prefix*10+digit, and contribute only when both children are absent.
Return the current number at a leaf; otherwise sum the recursive results for both children.
A missing child contributes zero, not an additional copy of the prefix.
editorial: A recursive call carries the number represented by the path before the current node. Multiply by ten and add the current digit to extend it. At a leaf, return that complete number; at an internal node, add the totals from the existing branches. The depth limit keeps the call stack small. The oracle independently constructs decimal strings from root-to-leaf path keys.
